3.diagnosis: Early LR sweep on LFM2 (frozen backbone + head fine-tuning).
3.citations: Devlin et al. 2019 (BERT fine-tuning LR conventions); Hu et al. 2022 (LoRA — low LR for adapters).
3.hypothesis: Lower LR than default 1e-4 improves head-only fine-tuning stability on small financial data.
3.learning: lr=3e-5 is the sweet spot for plain-Huber LFM2 head fine-tuning.

20.hypothesis: lr=2e-5 slightly lower may better fit regime transitions.
20.verdict: KEEP-but-unreproducible: single-seed +1.77 yielded champion; multi-seed median ~+0.11.
20.learning: Seed variance dominates single-run results on LFM2. Established need for multi-seed protocol for future champions.

66.citations: He et al. 2016 (Deep Residual Learning / ResNet).
66.hypothesis: A linear shortcut + nonlinear residual branch dominates on small financial data; the linear path anchors a regime-agnostic baseline, letting the nonlinear branch learn corrections.
66.verdict: BREAKTHROUGH +4.67 — 4-line code change jumped composite from +0.78 to +4.67.
66.learning: Architectural changes dominate HP tuning on low-SNR financial data. One skip connection beat 47 prior MLP HP experiments combined.

96.diagnosis: MLP residual champion reproduction with enhanced metrics (precision/recall/F1/MCC + trade-level CSVs).
96.citations: He et al. 2016 (architecture); Srivastava et al. 2014 (hd=0.15).
96.hypothesis: Reproducible exact match with champion Exp32 config.
96.verdict: KEEP — pre-LSTM global champion, exact reproduction.
96.learning: Deterministic seed=0 reproduces MLP champion to 4 decimal places.

108.diagnosis: First LSTM autoresearch baseline run (previous LSTM data from ablation only, 5-epoch non-SOTA).
108.citations: Fischer & Krauss 2018 EJOR (canonical financial LSTM, SOTA lr=1e-3, stacked 2-layer, bidirectional).
108.hypothesis: Classical financial-LSTM recipe with our proven training discipline (ep=50, pat=10, hd=0.15) should give +0.5 to +2.5 baseline.
108.learning: LSTM's temporal inductive bias is strong for FX returns even at seq=10.

110.diagnosis: LSTM with proper SOTA epoch count per Fischer & Krauss.
110.citations: Fischer & Krauss 2018 EJOR — their experiments ran 100+ epochs with patience 15.
110.hypothesis: Exp108's early-stop at epoch 25 was premature; more patience may find better minimum.
110.verdict: KEEP — LSTM improved to +5.06 via epoch bump alone.
110.learning: Per-backbone epoch counts matter: MLP 50 != LSTM 100. Literature SOTA epoch is backbone-specific.

111.diagnosis: LSTM with higher head dropout — regularizing prediction head while keeping recurrent capacity.
111.citations: Srivastava et al. 2014 JMLR (Dropout) — recommends 0.2-0.5 for dense layers.
111.hypothesis: hd=0.25 breaks the val/test tradeoff seen in MLP (regularizing heads fixes fold 2 without hurting other folds).
111.learning: LSTM recurrent bias + head dropout combine synergistically (not redundantly). Fixed fold 2 test -1.75 -> +1.66 WITHOUT sacrificing fold 7.

113.diagnosis: LSTM with 10x stronger weight decay on top of champion.
113.citations: Zaremba et al. 2014 (Recurrent NN Regularization — L2 for LSTMs).
113.hypothesis: Slight L2 bump smooths the optimization landscape further without changing capacity.
113.verdict: GLOBAL CHAMPION (+6.10) — current global best, fold 5 test improved +10.31 -> +10.53.
113.learning: Marginal improvement confirms we are at a local Pareto optimum; wd=1e-4 locked in.

114.diagnosis: Half the LR for flatter minima seeking.
114.citations: Lewkowycz et al. 2020 ICML (The Large Learning Rate Phase) — lower LR finds flatter basins that generalize better.
114.hypothesis: lr=5e-4 finds flatter basin -> improved val fold 2 (the consistent weakness).
114.verdict: DISCARD — composite +4.95; val fully 7/7 positive (+6.88 best ever) but test dropped to 5/7.
114.learning: Flat minima help val metrics but can hurt test when val/test regimes diverge. Lewkowycz framework doesn't apply cleanly to regime-shifted financial time series.

115.citations: Qin et al. 2017 (DA-RNN dual-stage attention); Graves & Schmidhuber 2005 (original bidirectional context).
115.hypothesis: Causal matches live-trading direction and may reduce overfit to within-window future-to-past correlations.
115.verdict: DISCARD — composite +5.00; val fold 2 hit best-ever +2.02, but test lost fold 2.
115.learning: Bidirectional LSTM wins on test; unidirectional wins on val. Classic val/test split — bidirectional captures more context.

116.diagnosis: Longer sequence for more temporal context.
116.citations: Bao et al. 2017 (Financial Time Series Prediction with seq=20).
116.hypothesis: Fold 2 (post-crash recovery) benefits from longer memory of pre-crash patterns.
116.verdict: DISCARD — composite +4.25; longer context hurt overall (loses training windows).
116.learning: seq=10 optimal for our n=2738; Bao's seq=20 requires substantially larger dataset.

117.diagnosis: First PatchTST SOTA baseline (transformer-based time series).
117.hypothesis: SOTA config (lr=1e-4, ep=100, pat=20, hd=0.15) gives reasonable baseline.
117.verdict: DISCARD — composite -1.72; transformer attention under-scaled at seq=10.
117.learning: At patch_length=5 and seq=10, only 2 attention tokens — far below the 4+ tokens Nie et al. report as minimum. Need seq>=60 for PatchTST to shine.

118.diagnosis: Stacked 3-layer bidirectional LSTM for multi-scale temporal modeling.
118.citations: Graves et al. 2013 (Speech Recognition with Deep RNNs).
118.hypothesis: Depth captures multi-scale temporal patterns not accessible to 2-layer.
118.verdict: DISCARD — composite +1.64; depth + small data mismatch.
118.learning: 3 layers overfits on n=2738. 2-layer champion confirmed optimal for our data size. Graves's depth advantage emerges only at larger n.

119.diagnosis: GRU cell comparison — 2 gates vs LSTM's 3.
119.citations: Cho et al. 2014 (GRU); Chung et al. 2014 (empirical gated RNN evaluation).
119.hypothesis: GRU's simpler gating has fewer params, may reduce overfit on small data.
119.verdict: DISCARD — composite +4.59; GRU achieved 7/7 test positive but weaker Sharpe.
119.learning: LSTM's 3-gate architecture retains more signal at n=2738. GRU's parameter savings don't translate to gains here.
